core_obligations: Argue by induction on the degree of the monic polynomial P (proof lines 4558-4559).
For deg P = 1, write P(T) = T - alpha and note that Q = 1 is monic and works (proof lines 4559-4560).

For deg P > 1, use division with remainder by the monic polynomial T - alpha to write P(T) = (T - alpha)Q(T) + r with Q of smaller degree and r in R, then evaluate at alpha and use P(alpha) = 0 to conclude r = 0 (proof lines 4560-4564).

difficulty_reason: The lemma is the first structural fact used in the section on descent of flatness along integral maps: a monic polynomial P over an arbitrary ring with a root alpha factors as (T - alpha) times a monic Q (statement lines 4551-4555). The author's proof is an 8-line induction on the degree which uses polynomial division by the monic linear factor T - alpha and evaluates the remainder at alpha (proof lines 4558-4565). What a reader has to supply is that division with remainder by a monic polynomial is available over an arbitrary ring, including over a ring with zero divisors, and that evaluating (T - alpha)Q + r at alpha leaves exactly r: the two steps are standard but they are what makes the argument work and the author does not spell them out beyond recording the division. Everything else in the proof is the induction, which is carried out for all degrees including the case where the ring is not a domain.
